trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering a waterfront facility, including its systems and data
deadline: Immediately
notify: FBI, CISA (for any cyber incident), and the Captain of the Port
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - PLT-01 (waterfront MTSA facility); the company reports under 6.16-1
clock_starts: Evidence of the incident (do not wait for confirmation)

obligation: MTSA alternative report to the National Response Center (C-CHEMICAL-R02)
trigger: Reportable cyber incident, for entities that have not reported under 6.16-1
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Fallback only - used if the 6.16-1 report cannot be made
clock_starts: Determination that the incident is reportable

obligation: MTSA breach of security or transportation security incident report
trigger: Breach of security at the facility; a transportation security incident (TSI)
deadline: Without delay (TSI to the COTP, then follow the Facility Security Plan)
notify: National Response Center (breach of security); local Captain of the Port (TSI)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - PLT-01 if the intrusion is a breach of security or leads to a TSI
clock_starts: Recognition of the breach or TSI

obligation: MTSA notice of temporary deviation from cybersecurity requirements
trigger: Facility must temporarily deviate from Subpart F requirements (for example, emergency remote access or disabled monitoring during recovery)
deadline: Before or as soon as the deviation starts; request temporary permission to operate
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - PLT-01

obligation: MTSA notice of exigent additional security measures
trigger: Company puts additional security measures in place for an exigent situation that are not in the approved plan
deadline: By the most rapid means practicable
notify: Cognizant Captain of the Port (nature of measures, circumstances, expected duration)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - PLT-01, once the Cybersecurity Plan is approved

trigger: Any reportable cyber incident or breach of security
deadline: Record during the incident; keep at least 2 years
notify: Internal (FSO records); available to the Coast Guard
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - PLT-01

trigger: Release of a hazardous substance at or above its RQ in 24 hours: ammonia 100 lb; chlorine 10 lb; sodium hypochlorite 100 lb
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge knows of the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all plants, whatever the cause (cyber or not)

trigger: Release of an EPCRA extremely hazardous substance (ammonia, chlorine) or CERCLA hazardous substance at or above its RQ with potential offsite exposure
deadline: Immediately
notify: Community emergency coordinator for the LEPC of any area likely to be affected, and the SERC of any state likely to be affected
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all plants

trigger: After an immediate EPCRA notice
deadline: As soon as practicable after the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an immediate notice was made

trigger: Need for emergency response to an accidental release from a covered process
deadline: When there is a need for a response, with timely data on the nature of the release
notify: Local emergency responders (911); PLT-01 hazardous materials team responds on site
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 8 RMP plants
owner: Plant manager (incident commander for process safety)

trigger: Incident that resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in, a catastrophic release (includes a cyber manipulation of ammonia unit alarm limits or setpoints)
deadline: Start as promptly as possible, not later than 48 hours after the incident
notify: Internal investigation team; report retained 5 years
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Program 3 processes at PLT-01, PLT-04, PLT-05
owner: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS

trigger: Incident that resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in, a catastrophic release of a highly hazardous chemical in the workplace
deadline: Start as promptly as possible, not later than 48 hours after the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - PSM processes at PLT-01, PLT-04, PLT-05
owner: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS

obligation: RMP root cause analysis for reportable accidents
trigger: Incident that meets the 68.42 accident history criteria
deadline: Report within 12 months, with root causes (applies from 2027-05-10)
notify: Internal; available to the implementing agency
applies_at_this_tier: Not yet - compliance date 2027-05-10; the 2026 EPA proposal (91 FR 8970) would revise it
owner: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS

trigger: Accidental release from a covered process with deaths, injuries, significant on-site property damage, or known offsite impacts
deadline: Within six months of the release, or by the next RMP update if earlier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the 68.42 criteria are met
owner: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS

obligation: RMP public meeting after an accident with offsite impacts
trigger: RMP reportable accident with known offsite impacts (68.42(a))
deadline: Within 90 days of the accident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if offsite impacts occur
owner: Vice President, Corporate Communications with the Vice President, Process Safety and EHS

obligation: OSHA severe injury and fatality report
trigger: Work-related fatality; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye
deadline: Fatality within 8 hours; hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss within 24 hours
notify: OSHA Area Office or 1-800-321-6742, or online
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a worker is harmed

trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material, including an OT incident that forces a plant to a safe state
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.6)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Attorney General delay provision); SEC Release 33-11216
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay only for the period the Attorney General specifies
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines (possible for an attack on chemical infrastructure)

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (for example, HR or payroll data or SL-1 portal credentials taken during the incident)
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed; the GC-PCBMS holds none, but the business network does
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employees and former employees are the most likely group)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida residents are affected
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no extension)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (about 4,600 current employees are in Florida)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent (HR and payroll SaaS, ERP, SL-1 hosting)
deadline: No later than 10 days after the agent's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound; tracked in vendor contracts

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Voluntary CISA and FBI report (plants other than PLT-01)
citation: CISA voluntary reporting; CISA RBPS 8 guidance (C-CHEMICAL-R01, voluntary benchmark)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed intrusion into OT at any plant
deadline: No legal deadline; company target within 24 hours of declaration (POL-03)
notify: CISA (cisa.gov/report) and the FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended; also an OFAC mitigating factor

trigger: Significant security incident at a covered facility
deadline: Not enforceable
applies_at_this_tier: No - CFATS authority expired 2023-07-28 and not reauthorized as of 2026-10-05; report voluntarily to CISA instead

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (proposed)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-05; as proposed the company would be covered

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

citation: SL-1 and SL-2 agreements (contract); SOC 2 commitments (P09)
trigger: Incident affecting telemetry data, toll customer recipes, batch records, or delivery commitments
deadline: Per contract (SL-2 agreements: 72 hours for incidents affecting customer recipes)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; check each agreement
owner: Vice President, Digital Services; Vice President, Toll Manufacturing

trigger: Incident that may interrupt water treatment chemical deliveries
deadline: Per contract; company target within 24 hours of a supply risk
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
owner: Senior Vice President, Water Treatment Business
